strings.name: Keir Starmer
strings.role: Former UK prime minister · Former chief prosecutor
strings.summary: Starmer moved from human rights law into public prosecution and parliament. He led the Crown Prosecution Service in England and Wales, became Labour leader in 2020 and took the party to victory in 2024. As prime minister he pursued energy and other public policy changes, but reversals, local election losses and party pressure undermined his leadership. He left office in July 2026 and later announced his departure from parliament.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Moved from prosecution and human-rights law into British politics, leading Labour to an election victory and pursuing a reorganization of government policy.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: University of Leeds, LLB (1985); University of Oxford, BCL (1986)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Labour’s return to government
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Led a change of direction after taking over Labour in 2020 and won a parliamentary majority in 2024.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Legal and prosecution career
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Worked in human rights law and led the Crown Prosecution Service from 2008 to 2013.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Announced his departure from parliament
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Said after leaving the premiership that he would resign as an MP and focus on international affairs.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Left the premiership
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Delivered his final Downing Street speech and handed over to Andy Burnham.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Announced his resignation
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Announced his departure after local election setbacks and party pressure, remaining in office until the handover.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Energy legislation enacted
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The Great British Energy Act received Royal Assent during his premiership, establishing a statutory basis for the public energy company.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Became UK prime minister
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Labour’s election majority ended fourteen years of Conservative government.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Elected Labour leader
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Succeeded Jeremy Corbyn after Labour’s heavy 2019 defeat and pursued a reorganization.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Elected to parliament
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Entered the House of Commons for Holborn and St Pancras after a legal career.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Became director of public prosecutions
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Began leading the Crown Prosecution Service in England and Wales and served until 2013.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Qualified as a barrister
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Entered legal practice, later specializing in human rights and advising the Northern Ireland Policing Board.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Completed his Leeds law degree
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Earned an LLB, followed by the postgraduate BCL at Oxford the next year.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in London
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Southwark and raised in Surrey; later became the first in his family to attend university.
